details.reasons: The candidate gets the order right: snooze, then dedup, then case creation. It covers the snooze matching and the `break` on an expired snooze filter, which stops later filters from being checked. It gives the 45-minute default from SIGNAL_DEFAULT_DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES, applied only when the signal has no filters, and notes the docstring still says 1 hour. It treats per-filter windows as seconds, with the 3600 column default and the 600 Pydantic default. Canary handling matches the reference: snoozable, never deduplicated, never a dedup target, and no case created. The candidate adds details the reference doesn't cover, such as the batch entry point and the null case_id claim in the filter branch. None of them contradicts the reference. The one gap is that it doesn't point out that the UI labels windows in minutes.
